frontier: A385316 a(6): smallest N expressible as sum of three prime cubes in exactly 6 unordered ways (p^3+q^3+r^3, p≤q≤r prime). Current OEIS table a(1..5) verified; lower bound 4.99e11 from prior census.
action:
Milestone: bounded_exact_search; contract=sha256:5c3f895292d59b11fc8f37a0f70c223f24ee5aa5a6d73b5948bfd5c1e9c4c69b
Implemented and executed a memory-optimized two-sum census mechanism: sieve primes up to C^(1/3), enumerate all pairwise prime-cube sums with multiplicity, then count three-sum representations for every N ≤ C. Ran at C=1e9 (168 primes, ~14K pairs) and C=1e10 (325 primes, ~53K pairs), reporting multiplicity distributions.
verified:
C=1e9: a(1)=24 (328,771 values at k=1), a(2)=185527 (2,269 at k=2), a(3)=8627527 (22 at k=3), max_mult=3.
C=1e10: a(1)=24, a(2)=185527, a(3)=8627527, a(4)=999979163 (2 values at k=4), max_mult=4.
All four verified terms match OEIS A385316 exactly. Mechanism confirmed: pair-sum counter + three-sum lookup produces correct known terms. Script: two_sum_census.py (CENSUS_SUMMARY stdout line for programmatic parsing).
result: Confirmed two-sum census mechanism works correctly for C=1e10 (325 primes, ~53K pair combinations, sub-second wall time). a(4) correctly identified at 999979163. a(5) and a(6) not found at C=1e10 — consistent with OEIS a(5)=10588881419 and the 4.99e11 lower bound. The mechanism is verified and ready for the full 1e12 census.
next_gate: Run two-sum census at C=1e12 (1229 primes, ~756K pairs) in a dedicated >300s session to resolve a(5) and search for a(6).
